download docker images. hello-world beginner ubuntu hello world is a compact end-to-end cradle example for beginners. it demonstrates how to combine scenario-local configurations and heuristics with modules from the remote cradle-lib repository, then run a local object as an event. the scenario is testbed-independent and has no committed deployment profile. what is included helloworld.cradle : the scenario specification, including its instance, network, module references, and event definition. local configuration : writes a readiness marker during provisioning. local cve manifest and ansible template : supply the scenario-local cve/cve-2021-44228 heuristic. event object : the script run by mainevent() . readme : the original setup and run instructions. topology preview : the supplied scenario illustration. the specification also reuses the linux-unzip configuration and the cve/cve-2017-7494 heuristic from remote cradle-lib . topology and exercise one ubuntu 20.04 instance, hello , connects to the private lan network ( 10.42.0.0/24 ) at 10.42.0.10 . provisioning applies the local readiness configuration, the shared unzip configuration, and both cve heuristics. the mainevent() phase runs the say-hello event, which executes the local hello object with bash without requesting root privileges. the specification declares preevent() and postevent() without additional actions. the exercise demonstrates module reuse and the provision-to-event workflow. after provisioning, the guest should contain /opt/cradle/hello-world/ready.txt . running the event should also create /tmp/hello-world-event.txt . runtime requirements install cxc and prepare a backend with an ubuntu 20.04 image. create an ignored cradle.toml in this directory to select the deployment target and dependencies. for vagrant with libvirt, use: name = "helloworld" target = "vagrant" [backend.vagrant] provider = "libvirt" [dependencies] hello-local = { path = "." } cradle-lib = { git = "https://github.com/cradle-lang/cradle-lib.git" } for openstack, set target = "openstack" and add the settings required by that deployment. keep deployment credentials outside the committed scenario files. from this directory, build the scenario: cxc build --output build run the boot, provision, and event commands printed by cxc, then check the two marker files described above. both cve
